scope: Native directory open/source/cookie ownership; resumable read-page composition; daemon typed jobs. Full Fuse service integration follows.
decisions: NativeDirectory is an engine-issued directory owner, using the existing FileHandle lease/reference semantics; no resident visited-tree map.

Directory parent relation is one indexed row per independently held directory and cascades on last file_custody deletion. Native lookup records the observed parent; R3 rename must update that relation atomically.
Cookie0 is start,1 follows dot,2 follows dotdot. Positive cookies>=3 retain exact name boundaries for this one open.

A bounded proposal reuses published name cookies and reserves distinct IDs for new names. Reservation is allocation, not enumeration progress; only accepted reply entries publish cookie mappings. Unused IDs remain holes, never valid offsets.
Concurrent proposals can assign alias cookies to one name, each valid; subsequent proposals reuse the first indexed published name mapping. No duplicate-name lifetime cap.
Each directory read has independent Source2 and a backed handle association. RELEASEDIR prevents new reads while existing sources retain cookie/header/metadata access.
After last directory-read source release, automatic maintenance removes at most64cookie rows per turn, then the closed header. Terminal logical close need not wait for physical cookie deletion.

Workspace merges the current local page with immutable base outside SQL using its existing64-key algorithm; entry kinds captured with local page or demanded from owned base; READDIR acquires no lookup count.
profiles: Overlay MEMORY/OFF/EXCLUSIVE; all Store executions explicitly Disposable/WAL/OFF. Durable NOT_RUN.
